# Deere & Company (NYSE: DE) — Strategy Scan, Construction & Forestry Focus

Note: Research done on 3 October 2026. Deere's fiscal year ends around 1 November, so the latest full year is fiscal 2025 (ended 2 November 2025) and the latest quarter is Q3 fiscal 2026 (ended 2 August 2026). Fiscal 2026 full-year results are not out yet.

## Company snapshot

- Deere & Company makes agricultural, turf, construction, forestry and roadbuilding equipment and provides financing for it, organised as three equipment segments plus Financial Services ([Deere 10-K, fiscal 2025](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/315189/000110465925122321/de-20251102x10k.htm)).
- Headquarters: One John Deere Place, Moline, Illinois; incorporated in Delaware ([Deere 10-K, fiscal 2025](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/315189/000110465925122321/de-20251102x10k.htm)).
- Public company, listed on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker DE ([Deere 10-K, fiscal 2025](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/315189/000110465925122321/de-20251102x10k.htm)).
- Fiscal 2025 net sales and revenues were $45.684 billion (down 12% on fiscal 2024), of which equipment operations net sales were $38.917 billion ([Deere Q4/FY2025 earnings release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/315189/000110465925116130/de-20251126xex99d1.htm)).
- Fiscal 2025 net income attributable to Deere was $5.027 billion, or $18.50 per share ([Deere Q4/FY2025 earnings release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/315189/000110465925116130/de-20251126xex99d1.htm)).
- Employees: approximately 73,100 at 2 November 2025, of whom about 27,000 were in the U.S. ([Deere 10-K, fiscal 2025](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/315189/000110465925122321/de-20251102x10k.htm)).
- Latest quarter (Q3 fiscal 2026, ended 2 August 2026): net sales and revenues $12.608 billion and net income $1.379 billion ($5.10 per share); first nine months net income $3.808 billion ([Deere Q3 FY2026 earnings release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000315189/000110465926098904/de-20260820xex99d1.htm)).
- Fiscal 2026 net income guidance: $4.75–5.00 billion, i.e. roughly flat to slightly down on fiscal 2025 ([Deere Q3 FY2026 earnings release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000315189/000110465926098904/de-20260820xex99d1.htm)).

## Business units

- **Production & Precision Agriculture (PPA):** large tractors, combines, sprayers and precision technology for production-scale growers of corn, soy, wheat, cotton and sugarcane; $17.311 billion in fiscal 2025, 45% of equipment operations net sales ([Deere 10-K, fiscal 2025](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/315189/000110465925122321/de-20251102x10k.htm)).
- **Small Agriculture & Turf (SAT):** utility and compact tractors, mowers, utility vehicles and golf/turf equipment for smaller farms, landscapers and homeowners; $10.224 billion in fiscal 2025, 26% of equipment operations net sales ([Deere 10-K, fiscal 2025](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/315189/000110465925122321/de-20251102x10k.htm)).
- **Construction & Forestry (CF) — the unit scanned below:** excavators, dozers, loaders, motor graders, articulated dump trucks, compact equipment, Wirtgen-group roadbuilding machines (Wirtgen, Vögele, Hamm, Kleemann, Benninghoven, Ciber) and forestry machines, sold mostly through independent dealers to contractors, rental firms, road builders and loggers; $11.382 billion in fiscal 2025, 29% of equipment operations net sales ([Deere 10-K, fiscal 2025](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/315189/000110465925122321/de-20251102x10k.htm)).
- CF is growing fastest in 2026: nine-month CF net sales were $10.079 billion, about 33% of nine-month equipment operations net sales (my calculation from segment figures), and Deere guides CF net sales up about 20% for fiscal 2026 versus PPA down about 10% ([Deere Q3 FY2026 earnings release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000315189/000110465926098904/de-20260820xex99d1.htm)).
- **Financial Services:** retail and wholesale financing of Deere equipment through John Deere Financial; fiscal 2025 revenues $5.821 billion (about 13% of total net sales and revenues, my calculation) and net income $1.114 billion ([Deere Q4/FY2025 earnings release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/315189/000110465925116130/de-20251126xex99d1.htm)).

## Industries and main competitors

Note: Deere's 10-K names 17 global competitors for CF alone; I picked the largest or most relevant. Strength/weakness judgements are mine, built on the cited figures.

**Industry 1: Construction, compact and roadbuilding equipment (Deere CF)**

- Caterpillar — Construction Industries sales were $8.346 billion in Q2 2026 (up 35%) at a 23.3% segment margin, against Deere CF's 12.1% margin in its Q3 ([Caterpillar Q2 2026 earnings release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000018230/000001823026000040/ex991toformcat2q2026earnin.htm)).
  - Strength: far larger scale and roughly double Deere's construction margin, with record company sales of $20.543 billion in the quarter ([Caterpillar Q2 2026 earnings release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000018230/000001823026000040/ex991toformcat2q2026earnin.htm)).
  - Weakness: construction is only about 41% of Caterpillar's quarterly sales (my calculation), so management attention and capital are split with mining and energy ([Caterpillar Q2 2026 earnings release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000018230/000001823026000040/ex991toformcat2q2026earnin.htm)).
- Komatsu — record first-quarter net sales of ¥1,043.1 billion (April–June 2026), with North America up 29.5% on data-center and rental demand ([Investing.com, Komatsu Q1 2026](https://www.investing.com/news/company-news/komatsu-q1-2026-slides-record-sales-beat-estimates-guidance-raised-93CH-4820701)).
  - Strength: strong global position in excavators and mining, and growing fast in North America ([Investing.com, Komatsu Q1 2026](https://www.investing.com/news/company-news/komatsu-q1-2026-slides-record-sales-beat-estimates-guidance-raised-93CH-4820701)).
  - Weakness: operating margin fell 0.9 points to 14.5% on tariffs, shipping and material costs, and full-year operating income is guided down 2.2% ([Investing.com, Komatsu Q1 2026](https://www.investing.com/news/company-news/komatsu-q1-2026-slides-record-sales-beat-estimates-guidance-raised-93CH-4820701)).
- Volvo Construction Equipment — Q2 2026 organic sales up 13% and adjusted operating margin 14.4% ([Volvo CE Q2 2026 results](https://www.volvoce.com/global/en/news-and-events/news-and-stories/2026/volvo-construction-equipment-delivers-increased-volumes-and-improved-earnings-in-q2-2026/)).
  - Strength: ahead on electrification — it delivered the first series-produced A30 Electric articulated haulers in the quarter ([Volvo CE Q2 2026 results](https://www.volvoce.com/global/en/news-and-events/news-and-stories/2026/volvo-construction-equipment-delivers-increased-volumes-and-improved-earnings-in-q2-2026/)).
  - Weakness: reported net sales fell 6% to SEK 21.6 billion after it divested its SDLG brand, shrinking its low-cost offer ([Volvo CE Q2 2026 results](https://www.volvoce.com/global/en/news-and-events/news-and-stories/2026/volvo-construction-equipment-delivers-increased-volumes-and-improved-earnings-in-q2-2026/)).
- CNH Industrial (CASE Construction) — construction net sales of $866 million in Q2 2026, up 12% ([CNH Q2 2026 earnings release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001567094/000156709426000015/ex991q226.htm)).
  - Strength: shares Deere's ag-plus-construction dealer model and is growing in North America ([CNH Q2 2026 earnings release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001567094/000156709426000015/ex991q226.htm)).
  - Weakness: sub-scale — construction adjusted EBIT fell 57% to $15 million on tariffs and R&D costs ([CNH Q2 2026 earnings release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001567094/000156709426000015/ex991q226.htm)).

**Industry 2: Agricultural and turf equipment (Deere PPA and SAT)**

- AGCO (Fendt, Massey Ferguson) — 2026 net sales guided at $10.1–10.2 billion ([AGCO Q2 2026 earnings release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000880266/000088026626000066/a2026earningsreleaseq2.htm)).
  - Strength: North American sales up 19.8% in Q2 2026, with market-share gains ([AGCO Q2 2026 earnings release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000880266/000088026626000066/a2026earningsreleaseq2.htm)).
  - Weakness: Latin American sales fell 25% and total sales fell 1% in Q2 2026 ([AGCO Q2 2026 earnings release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000880266/000088026626000066/a2026earningsreleaseq2.htm)).
- CNH Industrial (Case IH, New Holland) — agriculture net sales flat at $3.3 billion in Q2 2026 ([CNH Q2 2026 earnings release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001567094/000156709426000015/ex991q226.htm)).
  - Strength: guides 2026 agriculture sales about flat, against Deere's PPA guide of down about 10% ([CNH Q2 2026 earnings release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001567094/000156709426000015/ex991q226.htm)).
  - Weakness: agriculture adjusted EBIT fell 35%, and its full-year ag margin guide is only 5.0–5.5% ([CNH Q2 2026 earnings release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001567094/000156709426000015/ex991q226.htm)).
- Kubota — Q1 2026 (January–March) revenue ¥810.0 billion, up 13.7%; construction machinery up 28.6% ([Kubota FY2026 Q1 presentation](https://www.kubota.com/ir/financial/presentation/data/financial_results_26q1e.pdf)).
  - Strength: strong in mid-size tractors (new MX series) and compact construction equipment, which competes directly with Deere SAT and CF compact lines ([Kubota FY2026 Q1 presentation](https://www.kubota.com/ir/financial/presentation/data/financial_results_26q1e.pdf)).
  - Weakness: it reports uncertainty in the 0–40 HP tractor segment and lists U.S. tariffs as a profit drag ([Kubota FY2026 Q1 presentation](https://www.kubota.com/ir/financial/presentation/data/financial_results_26q1e.pdf)).

## Environmental scan

PESTLE for the Construction & Forestry segment only.

**Political**
- U.S. tariffs hurt: Deere's direct tariff cost was about $600 million in fiscal 2025, and about 80% of its U.S. sales are assembled in the U.S., with the rest imported mainly from Europe, Mexico, India and Japan ([Deere 10-K, fiscal 2025](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/315189/000110465925122321/de-20251102x10k.htm)).
- The February 2026 Supreme Court ruling that IEEPA does not authorise tariffs helps (refunds), though Section 232 steel and aluminium tariffs remain ([WilmerHale](https://www.wilmerhale.com/en/insights/client-alerts/20260220-supreme-court-strikes-down-ieepa-tariffs-what-now)). Deere booked $382 million of tariff recoveries in the first nine months of fiscal 2026 ([Deere Q3 FY2026 earnings release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000315189/000110465926098904/de-20260820xex99d1.htm)).
- Federal highway funding is uncertain, which hurts roadbuilding: IIJA authorities expired 30 September 2026 ([NACo](https://www.naco.org/news/iija-authorities-expire-september-30-naco-urges-congress-uphold-full-funding-levels-highway)), and a stopgap extends funding only to 11 December 2026 ([Union of Concerned Scientists](https://blog.ucs.org/kshen/extra-time-quiet-cuts-surface-transportation-reauthorization-extension/)).

**Economic**
- Non-residential demand helps: management cites infrastructure, data-center and energy projects, and rental makes up 30–35% of the earthmoving business ([Motley Fool, Deere Q3 2026 call transcript](https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/21/deere-de-q3-2026-earnings-call-transcript/)). Deere expects U.S./Canada construction equipment up 5–10% and global roadbuilding up about 10% in fiscal 2026 ([Deere Q3 FY2026 earnings release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000315189/000110465926098904/de-20260820xex99d1.htm)).
- Rising rates and soft housing hurt: the Fed raised its target range to 3.75–4.00% on 16 September 2026 ([Federal Reserve FOMC statement](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20260916a.htm)), and August 2026 housing starts were 1.275 million annualised, 1.2% below a year earlier ([U.S. Census Bureau](https://www.census.gov/construction/nrc/pdf/newresconst.pdf)). Deere expects global forestry down about 10% ([Deere Q3 FY2026 earnings release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000315189/000110465926098904/de-20260820xex99d1.htm)).

**Social**
- Skilled-labour shortages help demand for automation: 88% of contractors with craft openings say they are as hard or harder to fill than a year ago, and 58% of firms reporting on it say data-center work has increased competition for skilled workers ([AGC 2026 Workforce Survey](https://www.agc.org/sites/default/files/users/user21902/2026%20Workforce%20Survey%20Analysis%20(4).pdf)).
- The same shortage hurts project throughput: 42% of contractors say worker shortages delayed projects, which can slow equipment use and buying ([AGC 2026 Workforce Survey](https://www.agc.org/sites/default/files/users/user21902/2026%20Workforce%20Survey%20Analysis%20(4).pdf)).

**Technological**
- Jobsite technology helps differentiation: factory-installed SmartGrade adoption is up more than 50% year to date and jobsite safety solution sales up nearly 40% ([Motley Fool, Deere Q3 2026 call transcript](https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/21/deere-de-q3-2026-earnings-call-transcript/)).
- Deere is launching its own excavator models, rolling out over three to four years ([Motley Fool, Deere Q3 2026 call transcript](https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/21/deere-de-q3-2026-earnings-call-transcript/)). Until then it still buys Deere-branded excavators and parts from Hitachi under long-term supply agreements, which limits control of a core product ([Deere 10-K, fiscal 2025](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/315189/000110465925122321/de-20251102x10k.htm)).

**Legal**
- Right-to-repair is a growing legal exposure: the July 2026 FTC settlement requires Deere to give farmers and independent repairers dealer-level repair tools for 10 years. It covers agricultural equipment only, but it sets a precedent that could reach construction machines ([FTC press release](https://www.ftc.gov/news-events/news/press-releases/2026/07/ftc-states-secure-settlement-deere-company-advancing-farmers-right-repair)). Deere's 10-K lists right-to-repair legislation as a risk ([Deere 10-K, fiscal 2025](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/315189/000110465925122321/de-20251102x10k.htm)).
- Engine-emissions and environmental rules in the U.S., EU, India and elsewhere add cost to products, though Deere says compliance had no material effect in fiscal 2025 ([Deere 10-K, fiscal 2025](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/315189/000110465925122321/de-20251102x10k.htm)).

**Environmental**
- The push to cut jobsite emissions is both an opening and a threat: Deere plans hybrid-electric and battery-electric construction equipment ([Deere 10-K, fiscal 2025](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/315189/000110465925122321/de-20251102x10k.htm)), while Volvo CE is already delivering series-produced electric haulers ([Volvo CE Q2 2026 results](https://www.volvoce.com/global/en/news-and-events/news-and-stories/2026/volvo-construction-equipment-delivers-increased-volumes-and-improved-earnings-in-q2-2026/)).
- Forestry demand depends on the forest-products cycle: softer log and lumber prices are hurting forestry equipment sales ([Motley Fool, Deere Q3 2026 call transcript](https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/21/deere-de-q3-2026-earnings-call-transcript/)).

## Research summary

- CF is now Deere's growth engine while large ag is in a downturn: CF sales are guided up about 20% for fiscal 2026, PPA down about 10%, and U.S./Canada large ag industry sales down 15–20% ([Deere Q3 FY2026 earnings release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000315189/000110465926098904/de-20260820xex99d1.htm)).
- CF profitability is improving but still trails the leader: the Q3 margin was 12.1% (7.7% a year earlier) against Caterpillar Construction Industries' 23.3% ([Deere Q3 FY2026 earnings release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000315189/000110465926098904/de-20260820xex99d1.htm); [Caterpillar Q2 2026 earnings release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000018230/000001823026000040/ex991toformcat2q2026earnin.htm)).
- The upcycle is industry-wide, not Deere-specific: Caterpillar, Komatsu, Volvo CE and CNH all reported North American construction growth in mid-2026 driven by data centers and infrastructure ([Caterpillar Q2 2026 earnings release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000018230/000001823026000040/ex991toformcat2q2026earnin.htm); [CNH Q2 2026 earnings release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001567094/000156709426000015/ex991q226.htm); [Investing.com, Komatsu Q1 2026](https://www.investing.com/news/company-news/komatsu-q1-2026-slides-record-sales-beat-estimates-guidance-raised-93CH-4820701); [Volvo CE Q2 2026 results](https://www.volvoce.com/global/en/news-and-events/news-and-stories/2026/volvo-construction-equipment-delivers-increased-volumes-and-improved-earnings-in-q2-2026/)).
- Policy is the main swing factor: tariff cost, IEEPA refunds and the expired highway bill can each move CF results ([Motley Fool, Deere Q3 2026 call transcript](https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/21/deere-de-q3-2026-earnings-call-transcript/); [NACo](https://www.naco.org/news/iija-authorities-expire-september-30-naco-urges-congress-uphold-full-funding-levels-highway)). On the call, management put fiscal 2026 direct tariff expense at about $1.1 billion company-wide.
- Deere's advantage is technology plus dealers. SmartGrade, autonomy and the Wirtgen roadbuilding line give it a defensible niche, and in-house excavators would reduce its dependence on Hitachi ([Deere 10-K, fiscal 2025](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/315189/000110465925122321/de-20251102x10k.htm); [Motley Fool, Deere Q3 2026 call transcript](https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/21/deere-de-q3-2026-earnings-call-transcript/)).

## Suggested further research

- What will Deere's fiscal 2026 Q4 results and fiscal 2027 CF outlook (due late November 2026) show about whether construction demand is holding up?
- What does CF's market share by product look like (excavators, compact track loaders, motor graders) against Caterpillar, Komatsu and Kubota in North America?
- How quickly can Deere's own excavators replace Hitachi-sourced machines, and what does the Hitachi supply agreement cost it?
- Will Congress pass a multi-year surface transportation bill before the 11 December 2026 stopgap expires, and at what funding level for highways?
- Could right-to-repair rules spread from Deere's farm equipment to construction equipment, and how would that affect dealer parts and service profits?

## Limits of this analysis

- Note: Deere is a public company, so the main figures come from SEC filings and earnings releases and are not estimates.
- Note: Fiscal 2026 full-year results were not available; fiscal 2026 figures are nine-month actuals or company guidance.
- Note: Deere's ~$1.1 billion fiscal 2026 tariff-expense figure comes from a third-party transcript of the earnings call (Motley Fool), not from a filing.
- Note: Competitors report on different fiscal calendars and currencies (Komatsu April–June in yen, Kubota January–March in yen, Volvo in SEK), so the comparisons are directional, not like-for-like.
- Note: I found no reliable public market-share data for Deere CF by product or region; any statement about share would be [unverified].
- Note: The Komatsu figures come from an Investing.com summary of its results slides, not from Komatsu's own release, which I could not retrieve.
- Note: Strength and weakness judgements, and percentage shares marked "my calculation", are my own analysis of the cited figures.

## Summary

Deere & Company (Moline, Illinois; fiscal 2025 net sales and revenues $45.7 billion, net income $5.0 billion, ~73,100 employees) is leaning on its Construction & Forestry segment, guided up about 20% in fiscal 2026, while large-ag demand falls. CF's Q3 fiscal 2026 margin improved to 12.1% but trails Caterpillar's 23.3%. The key external factors are tariffs and IEEPA refunds, the expired IIJA highway funding, data-center and infrastructure demand, rising interest rates, labour shortages and right-to-repair rules.
